input: Research Peloton (onepeloton.com) for a hedge fund

catalysts.claim: Peloton's 2026 Annual Meeting is scheduled for December 8, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. ET; matters include electing a Class I director and advisory compensation-frequency voting.
Yahoo Finance's current estimate places Peloton's next earnings date on February 4, 2027 for the quarter ending December 31, 2026.
Peloton launched a proposed refinancing on November 9, 2026: a $600 million senior-secured-notes offering due 2032 and a proposed $200 million five-year revolver; closing and pricing remain pending.

results_vs_guidance.claim: Q1 FY2027 revenue was $559.2 million, $4 million above the midpoint of company guidance; paid Connected Fitness subscriptions were 2.475 million, at the top of the guidance range; gross margin was 61.3% versus 57% guided; GAAP net income was $96.2 million and adjusted EBITDA was $167.8 million.

The latest quarter's EPS was $0.19 versus Yahoo Finance consensus EPS of $0.10629, a 78.76% positive surprise; Yahoo's history does not provide a comparable reported-quarter revenue-versus-consensus figure in the returned record.
Current Q2 FY2027 guidance is revenue of $625-$650 million, gross margin of approximately 50%, adjusted EBITDA of $85-$100 million, and paid Connected Fitness subscriptions of 2.425-2.445 million.

Current FY2027 guidance is revenue of $2.30-$2.40 billion, gross margin of approximately 54%, adjusted EBITDA of $475-$525 million, and free cash flow of at least $350 million; the release says the revenue, EBITDA, and FCF outlook was unchanged from the prior quarter.
Yahoo Finance consensus for the quarter ending December 31, 2026 is revenue of $639.7 million and EPS of $0.02279, with 13 revenue analysts and 9 EPS analysts in the returned record.

event_driven.claim: The November 9 refinancing is the clearest current event-driven setup: Peloton intends to use the notes proceeds and cash on hand to repay all outstanding term loans, terminate the existing term-loan facility, and potentially use remaining proceeds for stock repurchases, acquisitions, capital expenditures, or other opportunities; the offering is not conditioned on the new revolver or the repayment.

credit_signals.claim: As of September 30, 2026, Peloton had $1.3422 billion of cash and cash equivalents, $350 million principal amount of 5.50% convertible notes due December 1, 2029, and $977.5 million outstanding under its term-loan facility; it had not drawn its $100 million revolver.
The term loan and existing revolver both mature May 30, 2029, while the convertible notes mature December 1, 2029; the term loan amortizes quarterly at 0.25% and bears variable-rate interest.

After September 30, Peloton voluntarily repaid $280 million of the term loan on October 9, 2026 using cash on hand, reducing the term-loan principal to $697.5 million and gross principal debt to about $1.048 billion.

The existing credit agreement includes a $250 million total-liquidity covenant and a $1.2 billion trailing-four-quarter subscription-revenue covenant, but those tests apply only while revolving loans are borrowed and outstanding; Peloton reported $40.3 million of restricted cash supporting letters of credit.

The proposed refinancing would replace the existing term loan with $600 million of senior secured notes due 2032 and a proposed $200 million five-year revolving facility; the interest rate and other note terms had not yet been determined as of the November 9 announcement.

alternative_signals.claim: Peloton announced a new Tread lineup including Tread Flex, added Peloton IQ features for runners, walkers, and hikers, and launched the Peloton Commercial Series; Commercial Business Unit revenue grew double digits year over year in Q1 FY2027.
Peloton opened ten additional U.S. microstores during Q1 FY2027, bringing the total to 19, and said it debuted the 'Let Yourself Run' campaign starring Miley in late September.

Subscription revenue rose $12.3 million year over year in Q1 FY2027, primarily from subscription price increases effective in the quarter ended December 31, 2025 and higher content-licensing revenue, partly offset by lower Paid Connected Fitness and App subscriptions.

Peloton's 2025 Restructuring Plan included a global headcount reduction and was substantially completed by June 30, 2026; the company does not expect material additional restructuring charges under that plan.
Chief Accounting Officer Saqib Baig notified Peloton on October 8 that he would step down effective November 27, 2026.

insider_and_ownership.claim: Chief Accounting Officer Saqib Baig sold 10,000 Class A shares on October 20, 2026 at $5.45, leaving 257,729.47 shares directly owned; the Form 4 says the sale was under a Rule 10b5-1 plan adopted September 2, 2025.

Chief Operating Officer Charles Kirol had 56,510 RSUs settle on October 15, 2026 and reported 28,849 shares withheld for taxes at $5.33; the filing describes the withholding as tax liability coverage rather than an open-market investment sale.

As of the October 14, 2026 record date, current directors, executive officers, and affiliates beneficially owned 2,075,984 Class A shares and zero Class B shares, representing approximately 0.3% of total voting power; Class B shares carry 20 votes per share.

risks.claim: The paid Connected Fitness subscriber base fell 9% year over year to 2.475 million in Q1 FY2027, and Q2 guidance implies another 9% year-over-year decline at the midpoint; FY2027 revenue guidance is down 4% year over year at the midpoint.

Q1 FY2027 total gross margin of 61.3% was partly driven by nonrecurring benefits; the 10-Q attributes the Connected Fitness Products margin improvement to IEEPA tariff refunds and the absence of the prior-year Bike+ seat-post-recall expense.

As of September 30, 2026, Peloton carried $79.0 million of inventory reserves, including $22.4 million for excess Connected Fitness Products, and had approximately $117.6 million of manufacturer inventory/component commitments due within one year.

The refinancing is proposed rather than completed: the company said note pricing and terms were still to be determined, and its 10-Q warns that insufficient liquidity could require additional debt or equity financing, with dilution or restrictive covenants as potential consequences.

Peloton identifies product recalls, product-liability and other litigation or regulatory proceedings, AI/data-privacy and cybersecurity issues, supplier concentration, tariffs, macroeconomic demand, and competition as risks that could materially affect results.

output.research_view: The setup is a balance-sheet and margin-quality trade: Q1 delivered strong GAAP earnings, adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow, and a $280 million term-loan paydown, but the subscriber base is still shrinking and FY27 revenue guidance is lower year over year. The November 9 refinancing could remove the nearer-term term-loan overhang and create optionality for buybacks or acquisitions, but the key near-term checks are whether the margin uplift normalizes without tariff/recall benefits and whether the proposed financing closes on acceptable terms.
